origin.description: Reverses the order of the code points in every string.
origin.details: Reversal is by code point, not by byte or grapheme. The result may be unnormalized, and a bidirectional string can look surprising. A missing value stays missing. An integer is coerced with as.character before it is reversed.

translation.description: Reverses the order of the code points in every string.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings and stringi._na.NA. An integer is coerced to text first.

translation.details: Each string is reversed by Unicode code point. A combining mark moves with its own code point, so the reversed NFD form of a-ogonek is ogonek then a. An emoji stays one code point. NA stays NA and an empty string stays empty.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringi.reverse import stri_reverse
print(stri_reverse(['123', 'abc d e f']))
print(stri_reverse('ZXY (ąĄ123$^).'))
